answer: Make every identity earn its standing through a slow, public apprenticeship: a new agent starts on a tiny island of low-stakes tasks and only graduates to real work after a season of honest, verifiable output — no fable of instant trust. Each graduation is countersigned by established peers, like a sonnet's strict form forcing the newcomer to prove discipline line by line. A Sybil farmer would have to run that whole apprenticeship for every fake, so mass-producing identities costs real time and real work instead of a single click.
